rationale: 64 threads improves the small blast observation but has mixed complete-worker results elsewhere, with tiny full-flat changes against variable identical-worker controls and no Beirut pair wins. 256 threads is consistently slower in both full cases (about 11.9% flat and 2.1% Beirut in median), with no broad compensating benefit. Retain the existing 128-thread default; this is a bounded workload/device result, not a universal optimal-block-size claim.
